Resolves #19820

A destroyed grid no longer leaves main-thread addon registrations behind.
- Every register arm that resumes after its `getAddon()` await now returns once its instance is destroyed. That covers the four `ScrollManager` arms, `VerticalScrollbar#addScrollSync` and `Container#addResizeObserver`.
- `addResizeObserver` reads both of its holder ids (grid and view, since #19804) before the await. An unregister that resumes after destroy therefore still names them.
- `ScrollManager#destroy` now also retires `GridDragScroll` and `GridRowHoverSync`.
- `VerticalScrollbar` gains a `destroy` that retires its `ScrollSync`.

Evidence: L2 (unit tests that record addon calls at the worker boundary through both doors, `getAddon()` and the `Neo.main.addon` namespace) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-4 are registration contracts at that boundary, which `ResizeObserverTeardown.spec.mjs` already pins). Residual: none.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). agent-preflight: not hosted here. The baseline ran: pre-commit hooks, `check-ticket-archaeology`, `check-pr-body` and `check-file-sizes`.
Prescription checked: `src/core/Base.mjs`, which owns the concern. The `isDestroyed` lifecycle flag is the guard. `trap()` is the same layer's alternative; see Deltas.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `AddonTeardown.spec.mjs` › a grid destroyed in the tick it mounts registers nothing and throws nothing |
| AC-2 | `AddonTeardown.spec.mjs`, all four arms: a destroy that races mount, a mounted destroy, a destroy after the hover flag was switched off, and an unmount and destroy in one tick |
| AC-3 | `AddonTeardown.spec.mjs` › destroying a mounted grid retires every registration it holds: the seven registrations checked before destroy |
| AC-4 | `ResizeObserverTeardown.spec.mjs` (as #19804 left it), green |

## Deltas from ticket
- Rebased onto #19804, which landed first. It registers the view as a second ResizeObserver holder and read `me.view.id` after the await, so its unregister arm also threw when the grid was destroyed in the same tick. Reading the ids before the await covers both arms.
- `ScrollManager#destroy` retires all four of its addon registrations unconditionally. Three paths could otherwise leave one behind:
  - the unmount path unregisters only when the manager has a `windowId`;
  - `rowHoverSync` has no hook that unregisters when the flag turns off;
  - the `dragScroll` hook unregisters only while mounted.
  An addon ignores an id it does not hold.
- The guard is an `isDestroyed` check after the await, the grid's own idiom (`Container.mjs`, after `passSizeToBody` in the resize handler). It resolves normally. `trap()` would instead reject through the global `Neo.isDestroyed` handler.
- Out of scope, noted in a defect-note: a grid constructed with locked columns never registers `GridRowHoverSync`, because `updateColCount()` runs in `construct` before `onConstructed` creates the `ScrollManager`.

## Test Evidence
Red first, in stages, on dev `3b3b26fff1`:
1. Unfixed: the race arm threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'horizontalScrollbar')` at `ScrollManager.mjs:286`, which is Ada's receipt. After the mounted grid was destroyed, `GridDragScroll`, `GridRowHoverSync` and `ScrollSync` were still registered.
2. `ScrollManager` and `VerticalScrollbar` fixed, `Container` not: the race arm failed only on the silent late `ResizeObserver` holder.
3. Everything fixed: green.

After the rebase onto #19804's merge, `git rebase` applied cleanly but put the guard below #19804's `me.view.id` read. The spec caught that: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')` at `Container.mjs:391`. The fix moved the read before the await.

Mutation check on the result: moving that read back after the await turns two arms red (the race, and the unmount and destroy in one tick).

Review round 1: the flag-off arm was red before `42f722990a` (`GridRowHoverSync` still registered) and is green after. All 311 grid unit specs are green.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

At `29e0408af9ca3198f0f2ca9b8b6271b45359548f`, ScrollManager.destroy line 165 calls `updateGridRowHoverSyncAddon(false)` only while `rowHoverSync` is true. The reactive config has no afterSetRowHoverSync hook. After a runtime column lock registers hover sync, setting the flag false leaves that registration held; destroy then skips its retirement.

An isolated exact-method probe extracted destroy and updateGridRowHoverSyncAddon from this head, with stubbed addon calls and Base destruction:
- register while true → destroy: register + unregister, held set empty;
- register while true → set rowHoverSync=false → destroy: register only, held set contains `GridRowHoverSync probe-manager`.

This is a method-level falsifier, not a browser or full-Grid receipt. The source registration path is Container.syncColumnLayout; the actual addon unregister is idempotent and removes the stored listeners. The requested native regression closes that boundary.

I also checked pending unregisters after Base destruction, the preserved window/holder IDs and duplicate unregister tolerance; no further concerns found in those paths.
